answer: Because the reef index resolves every citation against the zenith checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the wharf audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 199 aliases as a result pays the authoring cost 199 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 33 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
